###### If you travel by bike, remember to follow the ten commandments of good cyclists.

01. Obey traffic lights and signs. Remember: bicycles are vehicles on the road.
02. Remember that pedestrians have priority.
03. Use the bike lane whenever possible. If there isn't one, ride on the road in the same direction as the trains. Don't ride on the sidewalks!
04. Choose the right lane.
05. Remember to maintain a distance of 1.5 meters from vehicles.
06. Avoid weaving or tailgating other vehicles.
07. Always wear a helmet with reflective elements between 6:00 pm and 6:00 am
08. Avoid getting distracted by your cell phone or listening to music with headphones.
09. Show good manners, thank people when they give way to you.
10. Extend your arms to indicate where you are going:

**Right arm:** turn to the right

**Left arm:** turn left

**Arm up:** keep straight

## Subway and integrated transport system

500 meters from gate 4 (Block 19) you will find the Aguacatala Station of the Medellín Metro, from where you can access line A, which connects you to the center of Medellín to the north, line B to the west and line T to the east; and it also connects you to all the municipalities in the south of the metropolitan area.

![Imagen Metro y sistema integrado de transporte](https://universidadeafit.widen.net/content/f96c1839-418f-4db1-8c63-4ac85a81ef19/web/metro-350.jpg)

## Bus routes

At gate 1 (pedestrian on Las Vegas Avenue) you will find a bus stop with scheduled routes to and from the University that connect you with the southern municipalities (Envigado and Sabaneta), the east of the city (El Poblado sector), the west of the city (Belén sector, Laureles, among others) and the center of Medellín.

![Imagen Rutas de buses](https://universidadeafit.widen.net/content/5c7af62b-1da2-441d-ba2c-cc3914b8a01f/web/paradero-bus-350.jpg)
